hardware: lambda_63, 2x NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada Generation, driver 570.207 (GPU 0 only; GPU 1 and ~18 GB of GPU 0 were another user's idle llama-server)
env: conda env raytun3r, python 3.11.15, torch 2.11.0+cu128, opencv 4.11.0
what_this_is: The first real-network numbers from slambench. The raw baseline only: the fisheye frame goes to each model as it is, and the prediction is gathered at the release's own fisheye SLAM points. Nothing is rectified, warped, or depth-converted. rect_derect is absent by design -- camera.require_verified refuses it until the fetched calibration is shown to describe these frames, which it is not (see ticket 013).

split.egoexo4d: paused by owner decision, absent from this run

filters.note: the release ships UNFILTERED, so this cut is part of every number here

points_scored_per_model.note: identical for all five models, after the sigma cut -- every model answered at every point

frames_per_dataset.means: 8 takes x 25 frames, so min_points dropped nothing

oracle.role: the closing invariant, run on THIS split of the real release rather than on the staged sample
oracle.result: AbsRel 0.000 / delta1 1.000 / RMSE 0.000 on all three datasets, 600 frames
oracle.means: decode, sigma filter, gather, alignment and report contribute no error of their own to the main table

smoke.role: the ticket's CPU smoke -- analytic, aea, 1 take, 3 frames, --device cpu

comparability.across_baselines_of_one_model: the point of the harness, but only one baseline ran here
comparability.across_datasets_for_one_model: yes -- same model, same alignment space
comparability.across_models: NOT for absolute AbsRel. dav2_large aligns in disparity space and the other four in depth space, so its column is not on the same axis. The report's caveat is written blanket; whether the four scale_shift models are mutually comparable is a protocol question for the owner, not one this run settles.

observations: Oxford's median GT depth on this split is 15.07 m against 1.40 m (aea) and 1.57 m (nymeria) -- roughly ten times the indoor datasets, and about three times the ~5.3 m the data card estimated from a single sample take. Every model's AbsRel is worst on Oxford by a wide margin. Scene scale and difficulty are confounded here and this run does not separate them.
coverage is 1.00 everywhere, as it must be: raw answers at every point, and coverage only becomes informative once rect_derect runs and gives up the rim.
no frame was dropped for min_points and no model was skipped.
not_claimed: that any model is better than another in absolute terms -- see comparability
that the raw baseline is the right way to feed a fisheye frame to a pinhole-trained model; measuring that against rect_derect is the whole experiment, and the second arm has not run
anything about egoexo4d, which is paused
